subject: Closing pathway & MAP — evaluation milestones, pricing redlines
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Turner <sarah@cloudmedia.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP + eval plan proposal — next steps and terms to discuss

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — CloudMedia's ingestion patterns and peak playback spikes make for a great MAP candidate. I've attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (CloudMedia_MAP_v1.docx) and a simple pricing waterfall that ties discounts to committed monthly units during the evaluation ramp.

High level proposal:
- 8 week evaluation with three acceptance milestones (Week 2 throughput test, Week 4 quality check, Week 8 production validation).
- Discount schedule linked to committed monthly tokens (starter/scale/enterprise tiers).
- Quarterly true-ups on committed usage; initial price protection for 12 months from contract signature.

Can you confirm if the milestones align with your internal rollout? Also flagged a couple of contract items we expect CloudMedia to review: definitions of billable usage, price protection window, and true-up cadence. If you're comfortable, I'd like to get Legal on a short call next week to walk the redlines.

Attachments: CloudMedia_MAP_v1.docx, redwood-pricing-waterfall.xlsx

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | (415) 555-0136

From: Sarah Turner <sarah@cloudmedia.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP + eval plan proposal — next steps and terms to discuss

Ben —

Appreciate the materials. Overall the MAP looks sensible; a few items Legal and our procurement team asked to clarify before we lock down the timeline:

1) True-up cadence: we prefer annual true-ups not quarterly — our finance cadence aligns to yearly budgeting. Can Redwood accommodate an annual true-up with interim reporting?
2) Price protection: can you confirm whether price protection applies to all usage tiers and for how long after signature? We'd like 18 months if possible.
3) Definition of usage: Legal wants explicit definition of billable usage (e.g., how you count tokens vs API calls vs embeddings).
4) Escalation trigger: during the eval, if performance regresses, will there be a formal rollback to the prior model variant?

Our preferred next step is a 30-minute contract sync with your legal/sales ops and our counsel. Can you propose two slots?

Thanks,
Sarah Turner
Head of Platform Partnerships, CloudMedia Inc
sarah@cloudmedia.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Turner <sarah@cloudmedia.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP + eval plan proposal — next steps and terms to discuss

Sarah —

Thanks for the clarifying questions — great points. Proposed positions from our side:
- True-up cadence: we can do annual true-ups for contractual billing and commit adjustments, with mandatory quarterly usage reports (informational only) during the first 12 months of the deal.
- Price protection: we can extend price protection to 15 months on committed tiers; to get to 18 months we'd need to adjust the commit/discount curve (I've attached the waterfall with a 18-month scenario).
- Usage definition: Redwood bills by "billable tokens" (input + output tokens per request) and embeddings units. We'll include clear definitions in the SOW and a couple of worked examples.
- Regression / rollback: MAP will include a canary window and an automatic fallback policy to the previously-anchored model variant if latency or quality regressions exceed the acceptance thresholds.

Suggest we schedule a 30-minute call: Wed 3/25 10:00AM PT or Thu 3/26 1:30PM PT — let me know what works and I'll put Legal on.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-waterfall.xlsx

Best,
Ben

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: internal: negotiation tactics for CloudMedia redlines

Ben / Lauren —

Internal notes ahead of legal sync:
- Counter on true-up: accept annual true-up but lock-in a quarterly operational report requirement during the first year (helps with forecasting).
- Price protection: offer 15 months as Ben suggested; if they push for 18, require a 10% higher minimum commit for months 13–18 (waterfall row).
- Usage definition: include both token counting and a small protection for edge-case rate-limited ingestion ("grace tokens") to avoid disputes on spikes during onboarding.
- Contract language suggestions:
  * Define "Billable Tokens" = sum of input and output tokens processed by Redwood API for CloudMedia requests, excluding system/benchmark calls explicitly listed in SOW.
  * True-up clause: annual reconciliations with an invoice/credit mechanism 30 days after reconciliation.
  * Price protection cap: discounts/tier pricing held flat for protection window only for committed units; overage rates unprotected.

I recommend we prepare a short redline PDF highlighting those three clauses and a one-pager for the customer summarizing the economics. Priyom will own the draft (attached as proposed-contract-redlines.pdf).

- Priyom
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Turner <sarah@cloudmedia.com>, CloudMedia Legal <legal@cloudmedia.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP + eval plan proposal — next steps and terms to discuss

Sarah / Legal —

Following our internal alignment, attaching the one-page MAP and the redline summary for the commercial clauses you asked about. Short summary below so your counsel can scan quickly:

Summary of proposed commercial positions
- True-up cadence: annual reconciliations (customer-friendly), with quarterly usage reporting during first 12 months (ops-only).
- Price protection: 15 months on committed tiers; CloudMedia may opt into an 18-month protection if you increase the minimum commit for months 13–18 by 10%.
- Billable usage: defined as "Billable Tokens" (input + output tokens) and embeddings units; SOW will include worked examples and the list of excluded system calls.
- Regressions & rollback: MAP includes a canary window and automatic fallback to prior model variant if acceptance thresholds breach.

Proposed next step: 30-minute contract sync Thu 3/31 at 10:00AM PT or Fri 4/1 at 11:00AM PT. If those don't work, propose 2 other times and we'll adjust.

Attachments: CloudMedia_MAP_v1.docx, proposed-contract-redlines.pdf, redwood-pricing-waterfall.xlsx

Looking forward —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | (415) 555-0136
